reasoning_traces.think:
The evidence readiness matrix encodes a structured decision lattice where each factor's status depends on trust, freshness, and activation. Freshness ensures temporal relevance; activation reflects source adapter authority; sample size enforces statistical robustness. These combine into a Boolean lattice of readiness states. When all critical factors are ACTIVE and contribute, the system transitions to full inference mode. Otherwise, it blocks or defers. The dualities emerge in how trust and freshness interact—trust may override freshness if sufficiently high, while freshness can block otherwise valid evidence. Failure modes include stale evidence being accepted due to high trust, or insufficient samples being used despite freshness. The matrix thus acts as a dynamic Bayesian network node selector, filtering inputs based on their readiness to influence posterior beliefs.
